key_insight: T2D-Bench shows that clinically fluent LLM answers for type 2 diabetes can still miss required evidence, and an evidence-gated graph-based check can detect and repair those gaps.
clinical_relevance: For diabetes workflows, the framework highlights a way to make guideline adherence and lifestyle-related claims explicit, measurable, and easier to verify before use.
method: Built a multi-layer knowledge graph combining UMLS, DrugBank, SIDER, ADA rules, and lifestyle-to-glycemia links.
Evaluated LLM responses on 100 structured vignettes covering diagnosis, medication safety, and conflicting lifestyle advice.
Used evidence-path checks plus constrained revision to improve outputs toward verifier-level compliance.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% of GPT-4o-mini cases and 33% of GPT-4o cases.
watch_item: The benchmark depends on the coverage and correctness of the curated knowledge graph and computable rules, so gaps in those sources could affect what the verifier flags.
paper_title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
